channel.title: 1LINE Answers
channel.description: Real questions, straight answers: bills, complaints and scams, homes, gifts and family, and work.

item.title: I've been made redundant. What are my rights, and what should I do next?
item.description: Redundancy rights in plain English: notice, redundancy pay, time off to look for work, fair selection and the time limits, plus how to think about your next job.

item.title: How do I ask for a pay rise, and is it the right time?
item.description: There's usually no legal right to a pay rise, so how you ask matters. What decides the answer, what tends to go wrong, and the few rights that do apply in the UK.

item.title: Buying a house with no planning permission or building regs sign-off: how risky is it?
item.description: A loft or extension with no paperwork is common. Here is what the missing records mean for a buyer in England, how long councils can act, and the main ways people deal with it.

item.title: I’ve switched energy supplier. When does my old one have to send my final bill and refund my credit?
item.description: After an energy switch, your old supplier has deadlines for the final bill and any credit refund, with automatic compensation if it misses them. Here's how it works and what to do if it goes wrong.

item.title: What to get a man for his birthday when you have no idea
item.description: Stuck on a birthday present for him? Why men are often so hard to buy for, the kinds of gift that tend to land, where the clues hide, and the mistakes to avoid.

item.title: I don't know what to do with my life. Where do I start?
item.description: Feeling stuck or lost about your direction is common at 26 and at 51. Why it happens, what usually keeps people stuck, and gentle ways to start finding a way forward.

item.title: Section 75 or chargeback: can my card company get my money back?
item.description: When a seller won't refund you, the way you paid may give you a second route. How Section 75 and chargeback work, what they cover, and what usually goes wrong.

item.title: My flight was cancelled and the airline still hasn't refunded me. What can I do?
item.description: What UK rules say about refunds for cancelled and badly delayed flights, why refunds stall, and the routes to take when the airline goes quiet.

item.title: What to get your mum or dad for Christmas
item.description: Stuck on a Christmas present for your mum or dad? Why parents are so hard to buy for, the kinds of gift that tend to land, and the mistakes to avoid.

item.title: How can I tell if a Black Friday deal, delivery text or 'order problem' email is a scam?
item.description: Fake deals, parcel texts and 'problem with your order' emails surge around Black Friday. Here are the warning signs official UK bodies point to, how to check safely, and where to report a scam.

item.title: My complaint has been ignored, or I've had a deadlock letter. What next?
item.description: A company has gone quiet on your complaint, or sent a deadlock letter. Here's how the waiting periods work, when you can go to an ombudsman, the time limits that apply, and what to do if there's no ombudsman.

item.title: I’ve had a huge catch-up energy bill after estimated readings. Do I have to pay it?
item.description: Why big catch-up energy bills happen after estimated readings, how Ofgem's 12-month back-billing rule works, when it doesn't apply, and what to do if you disagree or can't pay.

item.title: My energy supplier wants to raise my direct debit, but I’m in credit. Can they?
item.description: Why energy suppliers raise direct debits even when you're in credit, what they have to explain, when you can ask for credit back, and what to do if you disagree.

item.title: My takeaway delivery app refused a refund. What can I do?
item.description: Missing items, cold or contaminated food, the wrong order or nothing at all, and the app says no. Here is how takeaway refund disputes work in the UK and the routes that remain.

item.title: How do I appeal a private parking charge?
item.description: A private parking charge isn't a council fine. Who you appeal to, the time limits, what usually gets a ticket cancelled and what happens if you ignore it.

item.title: My energy bill is wrong and my supplier won't fix it. What can I do?
item.description: A wrong energy bill, a surprise catch-up bill or credit you can't get back? Here's how billing disputes usually work, the 12-month back-billing rule, and when you can go to the Energy Ombudsman.

item.title: I want to change career but don't know what to do. Where do I start?
item.description: Feeling stuck but unsure what to switch to is common. Here's how to think a career change through: what you already have, what usually holds people back, and the UK careers help available.

item.title: My flight was delayed or cancelled. Can I claim compensation myself?
item.description: When UK flight delay or cancellation compensation applies, why airlines refuse claims, and how to escalate for free without giving a claims firm a cut.

item.title: My refund was refused. What are my rights?
item.description: Refund refused for a missing, wrong, broken or undelivered order? How UK consumer rights and card protections work, what usually goes wrong, and where to start.

item.title: What to get your partner for Christmas when you have no idea
item.description: Stuck on a Christmas present for your partner? Why it feels harder than buying for anyone else, the kinds of gift that tend to land, and the mistakes to avoid.

item.title: Why am I not getting any interviews after hundreds of applications?
item.description: Sending application after application and hearing nothing back? The usual reasons a CV gets passed over, what volume can't fix, and where to look first.

item.title: What to buy someone who says they don't want anything
item.description: "I don't want anything" is usually a clue, not a brief. What it really means, the four kinds of gift that work, and how to turn it into the right idea.
